newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy awaits EU letter amid reports of deficit woe.
newsitem.headline: Italy awaits EU letter amid reports of deficit woe.

text.p: The European Commission will send Italy a letter this week on how to reduce its budget deficit amid reports that state spending is set to overshoot further than expected in 1998, newspapers said on Sunday.
La Repubblica said nine other European Union countries would receive similar advice from the Commission, but added: "The warning issued to Italy is the most severe".
The newspaper headlined its front-page report: "Ultimatum to Italy."
European Commissioner Mario Monti told Ansa news agency on Sunday that a letter had been prepared but he did not give any details.
Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on state television he had not received the letter but believed it was "routine".

The European Commission provoked dismay in the Prodi government last month when it predicted that Italy would have a deficit/GDP ratio of 3.2 percent this year against an official Italian forecast of 3.0 percent.
Under the terms of the EU's Maastricht Treaty, countries must have a deficit/GDP ratio of three percent or under if they want to join the single European currency from its 1999 launch.
The Commission also said Italy's ratio would widen to 3.9 percent next year.
Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore, in an unsourced report, said on Sunday initial data pointed to the deficit hitting 4.2 percent next year unless additional budget measures were taken.

Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said last week he did not expect the 1998 budget to include more than about 20 trillion lire ($12 billion) of deficit-cutting measures, but Il Sole said the Treasury was now looking at a 25 trillion lire package.
The government is due to unveil its three-year programme of economic forecasts (DPEF) before the end of the month, which will indicate latest deficit trends.
The plan has been delayed while the government tries to establish a framework for structural reforms of the welfare state.
Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said at the weekend he would meet unions on Tuesday to discuss the issue.
Italy is the only EU country not to have presented the Commission with detailed covergence plans of how it expects to meet the Maastricht target.

The Treasury has promised to send Brussels the plans once the DPEF has been cleared, but La Repubblica said the Commission would complain in its letter to Prodi about the time it was taking for Italy to deliver the document.
EU economic and finance ministers are due to discuss Portuguese and Spanish convergence plans in Brussels on Monday.
They are also scheduled to hold their annual review of member state deficits, after which the 10 letters will be dispatched.

Italy's deficit was 6.7 percent of GDP in 1996 and the government has pledged to slash this back to three percent this year. It has introduced some 78 trillion lire ($46.7 billion) of deficit cuts in the last five months to meet that target.
But many of the measures are of a one-off nature and economists say social spending must be reduced to ensure heavily-indebted Italy stays below the three percent threshold.
($ = 1671 Italian Lire)
